## Architecture

sqlpipe moves data from Postgres to S3 in three stages.

A reader process connects to the Postgres database and streams rows in batches. Each batch holds a fixed number of rows. The reader passes each batch to the converter.

The converter transforms each batch into a Parquet row group. Parquet (a columnar file format) stores data in columns instead of rows. This makes the output efficient for analytics tools that read only selected columns.

The uploader receives each row group and writes it to S3 using multipart upload. Multipart upload (a method that sends a file in numbered parts) lets sqlpipe retry a failed part without restarting the whole transfer. The uploader retries each failed part before it reports an error.

The three stages run as a pipeline. The reader, converter, and uploader work concurrently to keep data moving.
